chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father who said:

I went to Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and said, 'Teach me a supplication for livelihood.' He said, 'Say: O Allah, manage my affairs and do not let anyone other than You manage my affairs.' I presented it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said, 'Shall I guide you to what is more beneficial than this for livelihood? Clip your nails and your moustache every Friday, even if by filing them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended act of grooming for increasing livelihood according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual supplication with physical hygiene as a means of divine blessing (*barakah*). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the routine grooming of nails and moustache on Fridays from mere personal care to a recommended act of worship that facilitates sustenance, reflecting the broader tradition of linking bodily purity with spiritual well-being. This practice underscores the holistic approach in Shia jurisprudence where mundane actions, when performed with intention, become avenues for divine provision.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from his father who said,

‘I went over to Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan (Al-Basry), so I said, ‘Teach me a supplication regarding the livelihood. So he said, ‘Say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Handle my matters and do not let anyone other than You<sup>azwj</sup> handle my matters’. So I presented it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> point you upon what is more beneficial than this regarding the livelihood? Clip your nails and your moustache during every Friday, even though it be by filing it’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from his father who has said the following:

“I once visited ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hassan and asked him to teach me a prayer for increased sustenance. He told me to say, ‘O Lord, take charge of my affairs and do not make others the in-charge person of my affairs.’ I mentioned it to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he (the Imam) said, ‘May I teach you something more useful than that for increased sustenance? Clip your fingernails and mustache every Friday.’”
